Merged and verified on live traffic.

**The forced runs on `main` at `208a0a5`** — four, all green:

- **One run, one item** — three executor runs, each settling exactly one, with two items pickable at once. [#1036](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1036) rolled, [#872](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/872) and [#1099](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1099) closed.
- **The chain fired** — [run 32369261049](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/32369261049) logged `- 1 item(s) still pickable — dispatched a fresh executor run`, and the run it started closed #1099 **22 seconds later**. Under the old loop that item would have waited for a tick.
- **The durable record is on the item** — `claudinite-task-exec v1 basics/task-janitor [#872] success`, written by the executor into the terminal comment.
- **The drain is decoupled** — now a 2-second dispatch job with no checkout, no node and no secrets, where it used to be a full executor run inside the tick's concurrency group.
- **The continuation skipped on every success** — the half worth checking, since a job that fired on success would dispatch forever.
- **Nothing was damaged** — the janitor's own sweep reported `0 armed, 0 running, 0 needs-human; escalated 0, reclaimed 0`, so the branch-vs-main claim race I ran before merging left nothing stuck.

Two paths the runs couldn't show, both covered by tests I watched fail first: the heartbeat's beat (needs a work step over 15 minutes; canon's longest is 300s) and the close-time release (needs an item blocked on the one closing).

Closed [#883](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/883), [#892](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/892) and [#924](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/924); recorded Step 4's completion on [#801](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/801), including that its `blocked` citation had been stale for three days. Conversation captured to `conversation-logs`.

One thing I'd flag rather than leave buried: I filed [#1096](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1096) for the `could not reconcile label "claude-automerge": 404` that every executor run prints, on `main` as well as the branch. It's fail-soft so nothing goes red, but `claude-automerge` is the asker's merge authorization — worth knowing whether that label is reachable at all.

> ⚠️ Still open: [#1096](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1096) (the `claude-automerge` 404, pre-existing, unassigned to any change yet). On [#801](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/801): the fan-in reporting item, and [#877](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/877) (the tick rename), which Step 4's closure has now unblocked.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, name the folders the change touched** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Leave out test folders, README edits, and above all any file whose diff is comments only.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

{"number":801,"title":"Migration to the work-item queue: two PRs, one same-day validation burst","body":"The phase plan for [tasks-dispatch DESIGN](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md) (§14 points here). Design constraints from the owner (2026-08-13): **fewest disparate steps, fewest approval points, and certainty the same day** — we do not wait for a nightly run to learn whether the end state works. Deliberately generating real work to push traffic through every path is explicitly sanctioned.

**Approval points: two.** PR‑1 (mechanism + canon flip) and PR‑2 (fleet flip + slot deletion). Everything else is forcing and observing, which the mechanism itself defines as ordinary operations.

Checkboxes track progress; each burst row's checkbox is checked only with an evidence URL appended beside it.

---

## Where this stands (2026-08-16 12:10Z)

**One member is verified end to end, agentic lane included. Twelve more are blocked on owner-only credential work.** Steps 0–2 complete. Step 3 is most of the way: the flip is merged and observed, the first member ran a real agentic item to `outcome:done`, and three defects the burst could not have caught were found and two fixed. The slot deletion still waits on the remaining members.

| | state |
|---|---|
| Canon | on the queue since #854; 12 clean scheduler runs overnight, 12 items to terminal state |
| Fleet | flipped by default in #888 (`17902b9`); **GCEC verified end to end**, 12 members still need a CCR routine (#916) |
| Slot machinery | still in the tree, deliberately — deleting it before members are verified strands them (see Step 3) |
| Design vs engine | DESIGN/sim current to §15.24 plus F24; engine at pre-review behavior — the catch-up is Step 4 (#883) |
| Open follow-ups | #916 (owner-only, blocking), #921, #892, #924, #883, #877 |

## Step 0 — rehearsal (done)

- [x] Simulator + scenario suite green in CI; coverage map names the live-only rows

## Step 1 — PR‑1 on canon: the whole mechanism, canon flipped (approval №1)

- [x] Label vocabulary, tick workflow (cron + `workflow_dispatch`), executor workflow, janitor re-target, dependency fields + `after` yield + `create-work-item`, F8 signal exclusions, canon flipped, gate green
- [x] **Approval №1: PR‑1 merged** — #854, `b30ef77`

## Step 2 — the validation burst (complete)

- [x] **B1 creation + first-item rule (S25):** [run 31899008771](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/31899008771) — 12 items #860–#870, each `task:blocked` wearing its next anchor
- [x] **B2 the roll + reasons on record (S1′):** #860 — one ask, rolled to tomorrow, reason on the item, no comment spam
- [x] **B3 agentic happy path + real CCR invocation + records (S2):** #867 — wake → claim → hand-off with nonce → **live session in 31s** → result + exec record → `outcome:done`
- [x] **B4 agentless path end to end:** #859 — wake → executor in 2s → claim → prework → `outcome:done`, closed in 26s, no session
- [x] **B5 the chain + yield (S4/S23):** #863 — yielded while `core/update` was live ([run 31913047785](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/31913047785)), then claimed and running the moment the upstream cleared; its work merged as #887
- [x] ~~**B6 hourly cadence**~~ — **dropped** (owner). `create-extractor` is `gcec/create-extractor` on GoogleCalendarEventCreator, the fleet's only hourly task; canon has none
- [x] ~~**B7 missing-secret posture**~~ — **folded into Step 3** (owner): every member reaches the flip with its endpoint token unset, so the posture happens on real traffic with no scaffolding
- [x] **B8 force-while-executing mutex (S15):** #871 — queued behind the executing twin, then got its own verdict on release
- [x] **B9 multi-executor lease (S7):** #873 — three overlapping executors, exactly one claim, one execution
- [x] **B10 follow-up fields (S17):** #872 — `Blocked-by` + `Not-before` created and held blocked by the tick
- [x] **B11 janitor leashes:** [run 31900490000](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/31900490000) — 12 blocked/rolling items, zero escalations
- [x] **All burst rows green**

### What the burst caught that the rehearsal could not

Four defects, none of which any simulator would have produced. Three are fixed:

- **#879 → #881 (merged).** Hand-off appended a second `### Context` instead of replacing the first, splitting the item's binding scope while `instructions.md` says to read "the Context section", singular. Every unit test passed, because each tested one call. Confirmed fixed on live traffic in B5's own hand-off.
- **#882 → #885 (merged).** Queue sessions wrote `[unknown]` where the exec record's slot id used to go — `instructions.md` never said what replaces it — dropping the join from a record back to its work item.
- **The task-path guard fired correctly** on a hand-built item naming `task.mjs` instead of `task.md` (#871): refused, converged to `needs-human`, nothing run.
- **#892 (open).** The terminal convergence is agent-discretion, and **both** agentic runs got part of it wrong — #867's record field, and #863 closing with no outcome label and no exec record at all. Proposes a `converge-item.mjs` the session calls with its judged outcome.

## Step 3 — the fleet flip, then the deletion (approval №2)

**PR‑2 is two PRs, not one** (amendment, 2026-08-15). The plan said "slot machinery deleted in this same PR"; that is unsafe, and the reason is in the code:

- `updates/engine-update.mjs` **replaces the mount wholesale**, so a file canon deletes leaves every member's mount on its next converge whatever that member's config says.
- `.github/workflows/` is the one path a converge cannot push — staged, and landed later by the apply stage.
- The two stubs call **different entry points**: `run.mjs` vs `queue/tick.mjs`.

So deleting slots in the flip's own release strands any member whose workflow has not yet landed. Keeping the slot code makes that window benign (`run.mjs` no-ops) and #888 makes it **loud**.

- [x] The pack update flow staged only the scheduler workflow, so `claudinite-executor.yml` reached no member — #874, `5ca4c35`
- [x] **Approval №2: the flip merged** — #888, `17902b9`. `dispatchMode` answers `queue` for an absent setting, so members flip with **no edit to any file they own**
- [x] **A member's converge observed** — GoogleCalendarEventCreator, 2026-08-16 02:00:18–02:00:25Z: both stubs call the queue entry points out of the mount, `taskScheduler` carries no `dispatch` key, mount `queue/tick.mjs` byte-identical to canon HEAD, and [15 standing items created](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/issues/918) (GCEC #904–#918). Last slot-era item was GCEC #903 at 00:09Z
- [x] **B7 lands here** — and the fault was **not** the unset secret the plan anticipated. `resolveEndpoint` fails at the *declaration*: [GCEC #908](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/issues/908#issuecomment-5305803329) parked `needs-human` naming `taskScheduler.endpoints`, no session started. `endpoints` was declared in exactly one repo in the fleet — this one — so the flip left **every** member's agentic lane dark
- [x] **Per-member mini-burst on the first member (B1–B4 + B7 + B3 agentic)** — GCEC: agentless lane ran clean from 02:00Z; [GCEC #908 closed `outcome:done` at 11:28:16Z](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/issues/908) via a live session started 11:16:12Z, its work landing as GCEC #923; [GCEC #907 `core/update`](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/issues/907) closed `outcome:done` 11:49:02Z, converging the mount through the queue itself
- [ ] **The other 12 members wired and observed** — blocked on #916 (owner-only: one CCR routine + `CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN` per repo)
- [ ] #921 folded in — DESIGN §8's force recipe yields an item `pickOrder` can never pick
- [ ] **Then** the slot deletion PR (slots.mjs, run-ledger math, exclusive claim, re-arm, `FORCE_TASKS` path, slot-conformance checks)
- [ ] The migration reports itself through the mechanism it ships: per-member fan-out items + a fan-in item `Blocked-by` all of them (S18 live) — fan-in closed `outcome:done`

### What Step 3 caught that Step 2 could not

Three defects, each invisible to the burst for a specific reason — and the reasons are the finding:

- **#906 → #907 (merged).** `queue/instructions.md` was never in the vendor set: `computeVendorSet` drops every `engine/**/*.md` behind a two-entry operational whitelist, and #854 added a third operational doc without extending it. That file *is* the behavior of a work-item session. **Invisible because canon runs the engine from its repo root, not a mount** — so no amount of canon traffic could show it.
- **#922 → #925 (merged).** F18's episode boundary was stated semantically and implemented over only the paths that already wrote a comment; the roll and the `needs-human` park end an episode silently, leaving a claim that outranks every future claimant. The roll self-heals via the leash (canon #860 sat unrunnable 17:44Z→03:32Z); the park never does. Fixed by *striking* the claim — including on the **losing** claimant, whose claim would otherwise become the earliest of the next episode. **Invisible because the simulator modelled the rule's intent rather than its artifact**, so it was correct by construction; the sim now models the artifact and reproduces the bug without the fix.
- **#921 (open).** DESIGN §8's force recipe — strip `task:blocked`, optionally add `task:urgent` — omits `task:ready`, and `pickOrder` admits on `task:ready` alone. A forced item is invisible to every executor and the run logs `nothing ready to pick up`, which looks exactly like a healthy run. **Invisible because no executable artifact pins DESIGN's prose recipes.**

## Step 4 — the work-as-work engine catch-up (#883; starts only after Step 3's verification)

#884 (merged 2026-08-16, `4380639`) changed the design under the shipped mechanism — decisions §15.14–24. **The behavior-by-behavior checklist lives in #883** — one box per capability, each stating what breaks while it's off; this plan owns only the sequencing:

- [ ] **Step 4 waits for Step 3's per-member verification** — the flip wave must be observed on the engine it shipped, not one changing underneath it
- [ ] Each #883 behavior lands burst-style per this plan's own discipline: a forced run observed on canon the same day; the workflow-touching pieces (heartbeat, decoupling, continuation job, suspend-all) additionally observed on one member's converge before the fleet's
- [ ] #892's `converge-item.mjs` is the natural carrier for #883's durable-record box — land them together, not twice
- [ ] #924 (a losing claimant's comment defers the leash reclaim) rides #883's heartbeat, which introduces the per-holder liveness signal it needs
- [ ] #877 (the tick rename) unblocks when this step closes — last, so the rename never churns files mid-migration

## Done means

- [x] All Step‑2 rows have evidence URLs on this issue
- [x] The first member flipped, wired and observed end to end — agentless and agentic
- [ ] All members flipped and observed; fan-in item closed `outcome:done`
- [ ] Slot machinery gone from the tree
- [ ] Step 4: the fielded engine matches DESIGN §15.14–24 — #883 closed
- [ ] 48h of ordinary operation as *confirmation* — explicitly not the proof; the burst was the proof

{"number":877,"title":"tasks-dispatch: rename "the tick" to a self-explanatory name in design and implementation","body":"Owner naming rule (2026-08-15, design-review session): prefer spelled-out names that read without contextual knowledge — single nouns like "tick" fail that test. Candidates discussed: `schedulerRun` (familiar, but collides with "the scheduler" = the old slot mechanism the design retires) and `generatorRun` (matches DESIGN §2's role name "the generator", no collision).

Deferred rather than done now, to avoid confounding the rename with the in-flight work-as-work amendments (#876): rename once the queue mechanism lands.

Blocked by #801 (the tasks-dispatch implementation tracking issue) — renaming before the mechanism exists would churn the design docs mid-migration.

- [ ] Pick the name (decide `generatorRun` vs `schedulerRun` vs other once the old slot scheduler's vocabulary has retired and the collision argument is moot)

{"number":916,"title":"Fleet enablement: every member needs a CCR routine + CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN before its agentic lane works","body":"Owner-only steps, one checkbox per repo. Blocks the agentic half of #801 Step 3.

**Done 2026-08-16 12:35Z.** All ten adopted members have a routine, a token and a merged wiring PR; their parked agentic items are re-queued and draining.

## What was broken

`taskScheduler.endpoints` was declared in **exactly one repo in the fleet: this one.** Every member had none, so `resolveEndpoint` failed at the *declaration* before it ever looked for a token, and every agentic work item converged to `needs-human`:

> Could not start an agent session: this repo's config declares no invocation endpoint "default" (taskScheduler.endpoints)

Agentless tasks were unaffected and ran clean throughout.

### The stored prompt — identical for every routine

```
Read .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/queue/instructions.md — or engine/scheduler/queue/instructions.md if that path does not exist — and follow it exactly.
```

## Per repo

- [x] **GoogleCalendarEventCreator** — wired first as the worked example (GCEC #921); ran a real agentic item end to end, GCEC #908 → `outcome:done`
- [x] **TLDR** — [#279](https://github.com/missingbulb/TLDR/pull/279); 6 items re-queued, all claimed and executing
- [x] **LaughCounter** — [#204](https://github.com/missingbulb/LaughCounter/pull/204); 5 re-queued
- [x] **CrosswordChat** — [#206](https://github.com/missingbulb/CrosswordChat/pull/206); 6 re-queued
- [x] **Sheepdog** — [#225](https://github.com/missingbulb/Sheepdog/pull/225); 7 re-queued
- [x] **EdFringeNow** — [#383](https://github.com/missingbulb/EdFringeNow/pull/383); 7 re-queued
- [x] **VascularColoring** — [#126](https://github.com/missingbulb/VascularColoring/pull/126); 5 re-queued
- [x] **ShoutsAndWhispers** — [#159](https://github.com/missingbulb/ShoutsAndWhispers/pull/159); 6 re-queued
- [x] **ClaudiniteCanary** — [#94](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary/pull/94); 6 re-queued
- [x] **MissingBulbWebsite** — [#165](https://github.com/missingbulb/MissingBulbWebsite/pull/165); 6 re-queued. Adoption **confirmed**, not presumed
- [x] **ClaudiniteWebsite** — [#186](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteWebsite/pull/186); 7 re-queued. Adoption **confirmed**, not presumed
- [x] ~~HelloWorldFlutterApp~~, ~~gRatio~~ — dormant since 2026-08-12; owner declined routines for them, so their agentic lanes stay parked by design

Every workflow half was **generated, not hand-written** — the output of running each repo's own vendored `converge-wiring.mjs`, landed via PR because `.github/workflows/` is the one path a converge cannot push. Each diff was exactly two added lines.

## Two things this surfaced

- **Not every parked item was parked for this.** Items were re-queued only where the task is *agentic*; agentless ones (Sheepdog #213 `fleet-add-missing-packs`, EdFringeNow #379 `edfringe/refresh-tickets`) parked for unrelated reasons and were left alone, as were slot-era `[claudinite-task]` items.
- **#929** — Sheepdog #213's park turned out to be a genuine regression from the flip: the queue stub dropped the `overrides` dispatch input, so the fleet's whole force apparatus (`fleet-baseline` included) refuses on every flipped member. Filed separately; it blocks the slot deletion.

## Not needed after all

The follow-up proposed here — landing the stored prompt as a tracked file so 13 routines get created identically — is moot now that the routines exist. Worth doing only if the fleet gains members later; #801 does not depend on it.

=== DESIGN §1-§3 ===
# Task dispatch without slots — the work-item queue

The mechanism lives in [`engine/scheduler/queue/`](../../engine/scheduler/queue/),
behind `taskScheduler.dispatch`. A continuation of the owner's sketch (2026-08-12, reproduced in Appendix A), played against twenty timed
scenarios ([SCENARIOS.md](SCENARIOS.md)) and the field's prior art
([RESEARCH.md](RESEARCH.md)), with the owner's eight decisions of 2026-08-13
recorded in §15 and folded into the sections they changed. The phase plan
belongs to a tracking issue, not here. It supersedes
the slot machinery of
[per-project-scheduling DESIGN §3–§5](../per-project-scheduling/DESIGN.md) and
amends several of its §12 decisions (each amendment is named where it happens).
What it does **not** touch: the task folder anatomy (§1), the precondition
contract, code-work and its secrets model
([task-code-work DESIGN](../task-code-work/DESIGN.md)), the outcome ceiling, the
security posture (the issue is data; behavior comes from tracked files), and the
usage-metrics records.

The shape in one paragraph: **work items are issues, available for work; any
number of executors pull from them.** A thin generator tick gives every
recurring task a standing work item at its anchor and flips blocked items
ready — pure label mechanics, no preconditions, no signals. An executor — a
GitHub Action by default, but anything that can read issues — picks up the
next ready item, claims it by label, evaluates the precondition (the only
place it ever runs): on a go it runs the work step and hands off to agentic work (a
CCR session invoked by API); on a no-go the item **rolls** — stamped
not-before the task's next anchor, blocked, reason recorded — so the item
itself carries "asked, declined, wakes at T". Follow-ups, fan-outs, urgency,
and one-off forcing are all just *creating or waking work items*. There is no
slot id, no run-ledger watermark, no exclusive claim, and no label-event
re-arm.

---

## 1. What the slot machinery costs today

The current design is push-shaped: one hourly scheduler run decides, at a single
instant, everything that will happen — which tasks are due, whether they run,
what they may touch — and encodes the decision into dispatch issues that a
label-event-triggered session then executes. Every complication below is a
consequence of that shape.

- **The slot id is state smuggled into a title token.** `d2026-08-12`,
  `h2026-08-12T14Z`, `m2026-08` exist so that a scheduled occurrence has an
  identity — which the exactly-once guard needs (title search per slot), the
  stale backstop needs (the *leading character* of the slot id is parsed back
  into a period, `SLOT_PERIOD_MS`), and forcing needs (the `~f<runId>` marker
  appended so an operator re-run of an already-run slot isn't silently
  swallowed). Three mechanisms each decode a fragment of scheduler state out of

contract, code-work and its secrets model

security posture (the issue is data; behavior comes from tracked files), and the
usage-metrics records.

number of executors pull from them.** A thin generator tick gives every
recurring task a standing work item at its anchor and flips blocked items

GitHub Action by default, but anything that can read issues — picks up the

re-arm.

{"number":921,"title":"DESIGN §8's force recipe produces an item no executor will ever pick","body":"Found by following the documented recipe on live traffic (#801 Step 3, GCEC #907).

§8 says:

> **Forcing a scheduled task is waking its standing item** … force = strip `task:blocked`, clear `Not-before`, optionally add `task:urgent`

Followed literally, that leaves an item carrying neither `task:blocked` nor `task:ready`. `pickOrder` filters on `hasLabel(i, READY)` ([`queue/executor.mjs:58`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/engine/scheduler/queue/executor.mjs#L58)) — `task:urgent` only affects the **sort**, never admission. So the forced item is invisible to every executor, and the tick will not rescue it either: its ready job transitions `task:blocked → task:ready`, and the item no longer carries `task:blocked`.

Observed exactly that on GoogleCalendarEventCreator: forced `core/update` (#907) at 11:11Z, the `task:urgent` label event fired the executor within seconds, and [the run](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/actions/runs/31943656688) logged `- nothing ready to pick up` and exited clean. A silent no-op that looks exactly like a healthy run — the failure mode §8 is otherwise careful about ("a force that finds no work *says so* where the operator will read it"). Here it says nothing to the item at all.

The engine's own re-queue instruction has it right — *"remove `needs-human`, add `task:ready`"* ([`executor.mjs:326`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/engine/scheduler/queue/executor.mjs#L326)) — so this is a prose defect, not a code one. §8 frames force and the §4 human re-queue as "the same operation on the same object", which is true, and then spells only one of them correctly.

**Fix:** §8's recipe becomes *strip `task:blocked`, add `task:ready`, clear `Not-before`, optionally add `task:urgent`*, matching §4. Worth checking whether the simulator has a scenario for forcing a blocked standing item, since S-coverage would have caught the divergence if the recipe were pinned anywhere executable.

Small enough to fold into the next #801 change rather than carry alone.

## 2. The shape — a pull-based queue of work items

Four roles, strictly separated (this refines, rather than replaces, the
2026-08-06 three-responsibility split — the scheduler's job splits in two and
shrinks):

1. **The generator** — a thin scheduled tick (the repo's one cron, unchanged
   rule). Three jobs, all deterministic label mechanics over the issue list:
   *instantiate* each recurring task's standing item when its time comes,
   *ready* blocked items whose dependencies have resolved and whose not-before
   has passed, and *reclaim* dead executor claims. It evaluates no
   preconditions and collects no signals (§5); it executes nothing.
2. **Executors** — any number of pull workers. Each iteration: pick the next
   ready item (urgent first), claim it, evaluate the precondition — the only
   place it is ever evaluated — then on a go run the work step and either finish
   (agentless task) or invoke the agentic phase and hand the item to it; on a
   no-go, roll a scheduled item to its next anchor (§5). An executor is
   platform-agnostic by construction: its whole interface is issue read/write
   plus the repo at HEAD. More capacity = more executors.
3. **Agents** — CCR sessions, one per handed-off item, invoked by the executor.
   An agent executes its one item's task file, verifies its outcome ceiling,
   and converges the item to a terminal state.
4. **The janitor** — unchanged in role, smaller in scope: dead executor claims,
   dead agent claims, stale-item escalation, queue health review. The re-arm
   retires (§11).

The queue itself is the repo's issues, and under the standing-item model that
sentence is complete: everything the system knows — including "this task was
asked, declined, and wakes again at T" — is on a work item. No plan file, no
watermark, no ledger read. The tick is a pure function of the clock and the
issue list; which is what the sketch means by *visibility into state*.

#916 is closed. All ten adopted members now declare an invocation endpoint, carry the token in both workflows, and have had their parked agentic items re-queued. Roughly 60 items released across the fleet, and **every one of them claimed on its first try** — no `claim-lost` anywhere, which is #925's fix holding at fleet scale rather than on one repo.

| repo | wiring PR | items re-queued |

| GoogleCalendarEventCreator | GCEC #921 | 6 (+ ran end to end earlier) |
| TLDR | [#279](https://github.com/missingbulb/TLDR/pull/279) | 6 |
| LaughCounter | [#204](https://github.com/missingbulb/LaughCounter/pull/204) | 5 |
| CrosswordChat | [#206](https://github.com/missingbulb/CrosswordChat/pull/206) | 6 |
| Sheepdog | [#225](https://github.com/missingbulb/Sheepdog/pull/225) | 7 |
| EdFringeNow | [#383](https://github.com/missingbulb/EdFringeNow/pull/383) | 7 |
| VascularColoring | [#126](https://github.com/missingbulb/VascularColoring/pull/126) | 5 |

| MissingBulbWebsite | [#165](https://github.com/missingbulb/MissingBulbWebsite/pull/165) | 6 |
| ClaudiniteWebsite | [#186](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteWebsite/pull/186) | 7 |

Both private repos are **confirmed** adopted, not presumed. HelloWorldFlutterApp and gRatio got no routine (owner's call — dormant since 2026-08-12), so their agentic lanes stay parked by design; that is now the documented steady state rather than an open gap.

Nine members needed no canon fix at all. The three defects GCEC bought (#906, #922, #921) were the whole cost of the first one.

## A new blocker for the slot deletion — #929

Triaging Sheepdog #213 (parked for a reason that was *not* the endpoint fault) turned up a regression the flip introduced and nothing had noticed:

The two scheduler stubs land at the same path but declare different interfaces. The slot stub has `workflow_dispatch.inputs.overrides`; the queue stub has bare `workflow_dispatch`. Sheepdog's fleet tasks dispatch that workflow **with** `overrides` carrying `FORCE_TASKS=…`, so on every flipped member the dispatch is refused. Seven members reported `not-dispatchable` at 06:57Z.

That takes out **`fleet-baseline`** — the fleet's force-a-member-to-converge lever, and the one this project's own rules require driving whenever a change to what members receive lands. It has been unavailable for flipped members since the flip.

Two consequences for this plan:

- **The slot deletion is no longer just cleanup.** Deleting `FORCE_TASKS` removes a mechanism these tasks still call, rather than removing something already dead. #929 has to land first.
- **The error text misdiagnoses itself**, blaming a disabled workflow or a stale member — pointing at repo settings when the cause is that the member is *current*. Worth fixing as part of #929, since anyone reading it goes to the wrong place.

## Step 3 remaining

- [ ] #929 — restore fleet forcing under the queue (wake the standing item rather than dispatch with overrides)
- [ ] #921 — DESIGN §8's force recipe (small, fold in)
- [ ] The migration reports itself through its own mechanism: per-member fan-out + a fan-in item `Blocked-by` all of them, closed `outcome:done` (S18 live)
- [ ] **Then** the slot deletion PR

The per-member observation row is effectively satisfied — every member has drained real agentic work today — but I would rather confirm the current wave reaches terminal states before checking it, and the fan-in item is the artifact that records that properly.

That comment reported #929 closed end to end on the strength of the `wake` dispatch working against `core/update`. The transport is indeed fixed. So a forced `fleet-baseline` item has been closed as obsolete since the flip. #971 fixes that, with a generic guard over every declared task rather than two point fixes.

`core/adopt-requested-packs` had the identical defect — the fleet's other operator lever.

|---|---|---|
| #929 | the scheduler's dispatch interface | Shepherd's fan-out tasks, sending `overrides` |
| #921 | the force recipe | DESIGN §8's own prose, omitting `task:ready` |
| #971 | forcing no longer bypasses the precondition | every `manual` task's precondition |

Each was invisible to the Step-2 burst for the same structural reason: the burst exercised the queue's *own* paths, and every one of these is a slot-era caller of a queue-era contract. # Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, name the folders the change touched** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Leave out test folders, README edits, and above all any file whose diff is comments only.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

- session-start-hook: Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code on the web. Use when the user wants to set up a repository for Claude Code on the web, create a SessionStart hook to ensure their project can run tests and linters during web sessions.
- adopt-claudinite: Bootstrap Claudinite into a consuming repo — mount, hooks, checks, skills. Use when asked to bootstrap, adopt, or set up Claudinite, or to baseline a repo to pick up updates.
- adopt-pack: Add one or more packs to an already-adopted Claudinite member — declare, run each pack's adoption interview, re-vendor, scaffold, land. Use when asked to adopt, add, enable, or declare a pack (e.g. product-wiki, executable-requirements) on a repo that already runs Claudinite.
- authoring-agent-docs: How to write instruction files coding agents follow reliably. Use before writing or editing any Claude instruction doc — a project CLAUDE.md, a convention doc, a routine spec.
- bug-investigation: Method for investigating a bug and pinning down its root cause. Use when investigating a bug report, when a fix didn't hold or a bug recurs, or when a report doesn't reproduce against main.
- bump-version: Raise the project's version — a minor bump by default. Use when the owner says "bump version".
- ci-performance-evaluation: Method for finding where a repo's CI time actually goes and what is worth fixing. Use when CI feels slow, when investigating a runtime regression, or when the weekly ci-performance task hands you a finding.
- do-later: File a change to be made AFTER the work in flight — a well-defined issue, marked for the queue and blocked behind the current PR/issue and behind the previous deferral, so repeated asks chain. Use when the owner says "/do-later …", "do this after this lands", or otherwise defers a change instead of derailing the session.
- extract-from-activity: Mine a window of a repo's commits, merged PRs and issue activity for durable, reusable lessons and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from repo artifacts — the growth-extract task's activity half, or an owner asking what a recent stretch of work taught.
- extract-from-conversations: Mine an agent-user conversation — a captured conversation log or the live session — for friction-driven lessons (misunderstandings, backtracks, measured wall-time waits) and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from a session transcript or the conversation-logs branch, or when an owner asks for a retrospective.
- file-placement: Where a file should live — the reference-distance metric, the high-reach code smell, and the mandated-location, test-location and plugin-contract exemptions. Use before placing, moving, or renaming a file, or when reviewing where one lives.
- generate-project-instructions: Decompose a project into its pack facets (working-style class, technology, aspect, domain) and extract its working instructions into reusable canon packs plus the project's own local packs (.claudinite/local_packs/). Use when a project has no established working style yet, or it exhibits a facet no pack covers — during bootstrap of a fresh/empty repo, or on an uplevel request.
- growth-dedup: Prune a repo's local packs of items the mounted Claudinite canon now covers — remove, strip to residue, or track a wording drift, never grow an entry. Use when the growth dedup task runs, or when asked to reconcile or dedup local packs against the canon.
- prose-to-checks: Mine pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. Use when auditing packs for convertible rules, when the weekly prose-to-checks sweep runs, or as the upgrade pass over prose a growth-extract run just wrote.
- repo-text-sweeps: Mechanics for grep/sed sweeps, renames, and path relocations across a repo. Use before a bulk find-replace, a rename, or moving files — and after one, to catch silently broken references.
- single-branch-status: Assess one branch's landed status — merged, already-in-main, superseded, orphaned, or genuine unmerged work — read-only. Use when triaging whether a single branch is safe to delete, judging by content not the ref's name (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-branches task hands you branches to assess).
- single-issue-triage: Triage one open issue and take the first applicable action — close-if-implemented, needs-decision, blocked, quick-win, or leave. Use when acting on a single issue; "implemented in main" must be verified against main's current content and the default is to comment, not close (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-issues task hands you issues to triage).
- single-pr-status: Assess one open pull request's landed status — keep-open, or closeable (merged, already-in-main, superseded, stale) — read-only. - verify-in-production: Decide whether a change that just landed can only be proven in production, and if so file the verification that comes back on its own once it is live. Use at the end of every change, beside the conversation capture — not on request.

Use when creating or editing a pack's skills/<name>/ in the canon; a consumer project's own agent docs are authoring-agent-docs' turf.
- writing-migration-plans: How to order the phases of an implementation or migration plan so nothing stalls mid-run — front-load the out-of-band setup, collapse the review gates into one stacked-PR pass, leave only executable steps — and how to keep its tracking issue append-only while implementing. Use when writing or reviewing a migration plan or a phased implementation plan, and when working through one's tracking issue.
- writing-tasks: The contract a Claudinite task is written to — the declaration's fields, the code-work and agentic phases, the precondition as the only decision point, ordering, and how a work item converges. Use when writing or changing a tasks/<name>/task.mjs or its worker, or when a task-declaration check fires.
- writing-tests: Practices for writing tests you can trust. Use before writing or changing any test — see-it-fail discipline, snapshot/golden rules, CI-only and heavy-browser tests, fuzzy-metric gating.
- design: Create a design canvas — a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.

Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Base directory for this skill: /home/user/Claudinite/.claude/skills/repo-text-sweeps

# Text & file manipulation

Portable practices for searching, extracting, and rewriting text across a repository's files — grep/sed sweeps, renames and relocations, and the silent reference-breakage they leave behind. These are project-agnostic; they're the mechanics half of editing a codebase as text. (General software-engineering practices live in [the basics pack's RULES.md](../../RULES.md); the merge-time relocation traps — git's rename detection, references that break with no conflict across a merge — live in [the git-github-advanced skill](../../../git-github/skills/git-github-advanced/SKILL.md), "Merging across a file relocation".)

- When you relocate a file's *content or responsibility* into a new home — folding a doc into a pack, moving a function to another module, absorbing a routine into a skill — the original is now **redundant surface**, and reducing it to a tombstone stub (`# retired — see X`) is not finishing the job: the stub still costs a read, drifts from its replacement, and misleads anyone who lands on it. Delete the emptied original in the *same* change, and treat "did this move make anything else dead?" as a standing question after every restructure — the source you copied *from* is the first suspect. Don't wait to be told a leftover is redundant; a relocation that leaves two homes for one thing isn't done.
- When renaming `foo/` → `bar/foo/`, a naive repo-wide string-replace of `foo/` → `bar/foo/` causes two silent corruptions: files already under the target namespace double-prefix (`bar/foo/file` → `bar/bar/foo/file`), and external URLs containing the string `foo/` get rewritten. Scope the replace to only internal path strings that need it, or do the replace then make a targeted post-pass reverting matches inside URLs and already-correct paths.
- A grep/sed rename pass over a path (`foo/bar/baz.js`) won't match it when built from `path.join` segments (`path.join(__dirname, "foo", "bar", "baz.js")`) or wrapped across a line in a comment — those references survive the rewrite and break only at run time. After a mechanical path-rename pass, also search for the path's individual segment tokens and run the test suite; the test suite, not the grep, surfaces a missed reference.
- An ordered specific→catch-all path rewrite can half-convert a reference the specific rule's trailing slash missed. Renaming `old/sub/` → `new/leaf/` with a slash-anchored rule (`s#old/sub/#new/leaf/#`) plus a catch-all for the parent (`s#old/#new/#`), a reference *without* the trailing slash (`path.join(root, "old/sub")`, a bare `git add old/sub`, a prose mention) escapes the specific rule, and the catch-all then rewrites only its **parent** — `old/sub` → `new/sub`, not `new/leaf` — a half-converted path that breaks at run time, not at the rewrite. Match both the slashed and bare forms, then grep the bare-dir form (at a quote / paren / line-end) and run the tests.
- After `git mv`, re-read the file at its **new** path before rewriting it — an editing tool that tracks reads by path treats the moved path as never-seen and silently refuses the write, leaving the file stale (a failure that surfaces much later, far from its cause). When the move and the rewrite share a batch of tool calls, check each result individually; a single refused write is easy to miss in a batch.
- To exclude a directory's own files from a reference search, filter by file **path**, not `grep -v` on line content: `grep -rn foo/bar | grep -v foo/bar/` (meant to drop the directory's own files) *also* drops every legitimate full-path reference elsewhere, silently undercounting. Exclude by pathspec instead — `git grep -n foo/bar -- . ':(exclude)foo/bar'` — which filters on which file is searched, not on what each matching line happens to contain.
- To exclude vendored, synced, or generated files from a **structural** check that walks a tree (an orphan/reachability scan, a doc audit, a lint), derive the file set from git's tracked list (e.g. `git ls-files`) rather than a filesystem walk with a hardcoded path to skip — it can't desync when the artifact moves, and it stays correct when a new ignored directory appears. (Sibling of the pathspec-exclude rule above: that one separates a directory from its own files within a search; this one separates owned content from vendored/generated content.)
- A zero-hit grep proves absence only at the case you searched. Code normalizes tokens away from prose case — an uppercase data table (`'KNEW'`), a SCREAMING_SNAKE constant, a lowercased slug — so a case-sensitive `grep knew` finds nothing and reads as "not in the codebase" while the entry sits right there, and a conclusion built on that phantom absence compounds. Before concluding a token is absent, re-run with `-i`; when history should have touched it, `git log -S<token>` is the cross-check that catches the miss.
- When writing file content captured from a script or command output, use the `Write` tool directly — never `cp` from an internal Claude Code path (`/root/.claude/projects/...`). The tool-results paths are harness-internal and inaccessible to shell commands; referencing them via Bash triggers a permission prompt. Capture the output in context and pass it to `Write`.

input.title: The janitor's stateless-item repair races the executor's own label swap and parks finished work
input.body:
Found on live traffic while proving S18 for #801 (the fan-in box).

`sweepQueue` reads the open set once ([`queue-sweep.mjs:32`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/packs/basics/tasks/task-janitor/queue-sweep.mjs#L32)) and then escalates from that snapshot. `statelessItems` admits any open item wearing no state label and no `needs-human` — which is exactly what an item looks like **during** a label swap, not only after one tore. The two are indistinguishable from a snapshot, and the sweep never re-reads.

Observed on canon:

| time | what |
|---|---|
| 12:50:09Z | executor `actions-32370886572` claims #1101 |
| 12:50:11Z | exec record written |
| 12:50:13Z | #1101 **closed**, `task:done` |
| 12:50:21Z | the janitor comments *"This work item carries no state label at all"* and adds `needs-human` + `task:needs-human-decision` |

[#1101](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1101) ended up closed while wearing `task:done`, `needs-human` and `task:needs-human-decision` at once, plus a comment asking a human to re-queue work that had already succeeded.

Two reasons this is worth fixing rather than tolerating:

- **`needs-human` is a triage signal, and this makes a false one.** It is what the health review counts, what `tidy-issues` reads, and what a person scans. A park filed against finished work costs a human read every time.
- **#1089 made the window much wider.** One item per run plus the re-dispatch chain means claim→close now takes ~4 seconds and executors run back to back, so the swap is in flight far more of the time than it was under the batching loop.

**Fix:** confirm before acting. The stateless rule is the one whose entire premise is "the state I am reading is torn", so it is the one that must re-read the item immediately before writing — skip it if it has since closed or acquired a label. The same read-swap-confirm discipline the claim lease already uses. The other three rules turn on a clock rather than on a transient, so they do not need it.

---

    cannot push (§14) — so every member spends a window running the refreshed
    mount from the old workflow, and a missing entry point there is a queue that
    stops with no run left to fix it. `scheduler-workflow-shape` accepts either
    spelling for the same reason. Both retire when no member's workflow still
    names `tick.mjs` — read the members' files, do not guess a date.
"""
assert anchor in s
s = s.replace(anchor, "\n" + add + anchor)

input.title: The tick becomes the scheduler run, and the janitor stops parking finished work
input.body:
Two commits, both out of #801's remaining work.

## `tick` → `schedulerRun` (#877)

`schedulerRun` over `generatorRun`: the slot scheduler was deleted in #993, so the collision that deferred this is gone and the word names one thing again — the repo's one cron workflow, which is what runs it. "The generator" stays the *role's* name in DESIGN §2 and §5; a run of it is better named for the thing an operator looks at in the Actions tab. Recorded as DESIGN decision 27, closing decision 21.

**`queue/tick.mjs` survives as an entry-point shim, and has to.** A member's `.github/workflows/claudinite-scheduler.yml` names the module by literal path, and that file is the one path a converge cannot push — it is staged and lands as a pull request somebody merges. So every member spends a window running the refreshed mount from the old workflow, and a missing entry point there is not a broken task: it is that repo's whole queue stopping, with no run left to notice it. `scheduler-workflow-shape` accepts either spelling for the same window. Both retire when no member's workflow still names `tick.mjs` — read the files, don't guess a date.

I did **not** delete `docs/per-project-scheduling/` — see the note at the bottom.

## The janitor's stateless repair (#1104)

Found on live traffic while proving S18 for #801. The sweep ruled over a snapshot of the open set, and an item **mid-swap** is indistinguishable from one whose swap tore, so an executor that settled an item inside that window got its finished work parked `needs-human`. #1101 ended up closed while wearing `task:done`, `needs-human` and `task:needs-human-decision` at once, with a comment asking a human to re-queue work that had already succeeded. #1089 widened the window a lot: claim→close is now ~4 seconds and executors run back to back.

The fix is confirm-before-act — re-read the item immediately before writing, and let a settled one go. Only this rule needs it; the other three turn on a clock rather than on a transient.

## Folders

- **`engine/scheduler/`** — `queue/tick.mjs` → `queue/scheduler-run.mjs` (`planTick` → `planSchedulerRun`, `main` exported as `runSchedulerRun`), a new shim at the old path, and `stubs/claudinite-tick.yml` → `stubs/claudinite-scheduler.yml`.
- **`.github/workflows/`** — the scheduler workflow's job id, concurrency group and `run:` line follow the stub.
- **`packs/basics/`** — the janitor's stateless repair now confirms before acting.
- **`packs/claudinite-lifecycle/`** — `scheduler-workflow-shape` accepts either entry-point spelling.
- **`docs/tasks-dispatch/`** — DESIGN decision 27, the vocabulary across DESIGN/SCENARIOS/RESEARCH, and the simulator's own `schedulerRun` and `scheduler-run-drain` trigger token.
- **`vendoring/rehearsal/`** — the `old-workflows` fixture keeps the genuine old text, so it now also covers the un-converged `tick.mjs` entry point.
- **`updates/`** — `stubFor()` follows the stub rename; `updates/` is fetched fresh from canon each converge, so both sides move together.
- Six pack versions bumped for the edits above.

## One thing I did not do

The instruction was to remove `docs/per-project-scheduling/` if it is all obsolete. **It isn't**, so I left it. About 45 live source files cite it as the authority for contracts the queue explicitly did not replace — `task-contract.mjs` (§1, the declaration contract), `calendar.mjs` (§2, the anchors), `discover.mjs`/`hash-minute.mjs`/`signals/*` (§3), `verify-outcome.mjs` (the outcome ceiling), and every pack's task header (§6, the classification table). tasks-dispatch DESIGN's own opening names those as untouched and supersedes only §3–§5's slot machinery. `MIGRATION.md` beside it is the dated record of migration #394, which `.claudinite-checks.json` already waives on the grounds that rewriting it would falsify the record.

What is genuinely stale there is narrower than the directory: the slot sections describe a mechanism that no longer exists. Worth a separate pass that lifts the still-live contracts into their own home and retires the rest — happy to open that if you want it, but it is not a delete.

## Verification

- 2347 tests pass; the janitor fix was watched failing without its guard (2 of the new tests) before it was committed.
- `check_the_work` clean, `check_the_world` 0 blocking.
- S18 and the close-time release proven live on canon at `208a0a5` — #1101 and #1102 fanned out, #1103 was `Blocked-by` both and stayed blocked until *"Released: #1102 has closed, and nothing else holds this item"* at 12:50:29Z, then ran and closed 25 seconds later. Whole cascade: 67 seconds. That was the one path #883 could not show.

Closes #877
Closes #1104
Refs #801

| 12:49:47Z | [#1101](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1101) and [#1102](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1102) created `task:ready`; [#1103](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1103) created `task:blocked`, `Blocked-by: #1101, #1102` |
| 12:50:13Z | #1101 closed `task:done` — #1103 **stays blocked**, one blocker left |
| 12:50:29Z | #1102 closes → #1103: *"Released: #1102 has closed, and nothing else holds this item"* |
| 12:50:49Z | #1103 claimed by `actions-32370949199` |
| 12:50:54Z | #1103 closed `task:done`, exec record on the item |

The release is the line that matters: it came from the **closing side**, not from a scheduler run. Under the pre-#883 engine the fan-in would have waited up to an hour for the next cron. This closes the box **and** the close-time-release gap I flagged on #883.

### What it caught that no test had — #1104

The janitor parked #1101 `needs-human` **eight seconds after that item closed clean**. Its stateless-item repair rules over a snapshot of the open set, and an item mid-swap is indistinguishable from one whose swap tore. So finished work got a triage label and a comment asking a human to re-queue it.

Fourth instance of this plan's own recurring class, and worth adding to the table in the 08-17 comment: **a contract changed and a caller was not swept** — here the contract is *how long an item stays stateless*, which #1089 cut from seconds-under-a-batching-loop to ~4 seconds with runs back to back. Invisible to every earlier burst because the executor was slow enough that the window rarely overlapped a sweep. Fixed in [#1108](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1108) by confirming before acting; #1101's false labels are removed.

### Step 4's remaining box is blocked on repo access, not on work

> the workflow-touching pieces (heartbeat, decoupling, continuation job, suspend-all) additionally observed on one member's converge before the fleet's

**#1089 has reached no member.** I checked GoogleCalendarEventCreator directly: its mount carries no `heartbeat.mjs`, `suspend.mjs`, `readiness.mjs` or `converge-item.mjs`, its executor workflow is still `timeout-minutes: 50`, and its scheduler workflow still runs an executor inline in the drain. This repo's own rules require forcing delivery in the same session for a change that touches stubs and workflows, and I did not do it when #1089 merged — that was a miss.

I tried to fix it here and **cannot from this session**: `missingbulb/Shepherd` is outside its repo scope, and attaching it was denied. So this is yours to press, or mine once Shepherd is attached:

```
Actions → Claudinite scheduler → Run workflow → wake: fleet-baseline
(on missingbulb/Shepherd, main)
```

Tonight's 02:00Z converge delivers the mount half on its own; the workflow half lands as a per-member pull request either way.

- [x] The fan-in item — S18 and the close-time release proven live, above
- [ ] #1089's workflow pieces observed on one member — blocked on the dispatch above, not on work
- [x] #877 (the scheduler-run rename) — done in [#1108](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1108); it was this step's last dependent

input.body:
Unblocked by #883 closing, and done in [#1108](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1108).

**The name is `schedulerRun`** (owner, 2026-08-20). The collision argument that deferred this is gone — the slot scheduler was deleted in #993, so "scheduler" names one thing again, and what it names is exactly the repo's one cron workflow `claudinite-scheduler.yml`, which is what runs it. `generatorRun` was the alternative and was declined: DESIGN §2 and §5 already call the *role* the generator, and a run is better named for the thing an operator looks at in the Actions tab than for the role behind it. Recorded as DESIGN decision 27, closing decision 21.

Both boxes are done: `queue/tick.mjs` → `queue/scheduler-run.mjs`, `planTick` → `planSchedulerRun`, `stubs/claudinite-tick.yml` → `stubs/claudinite-scheduler.yml`, and the vocabulary swept across `docs/tasks-dispatch/` (DESIGN, SCENARIOS, RESEARCH, sim code, tests and README), the implementation, the workflows and the pack prose that referenced it.

**One deliberate exception to the closing condition.** `queue/tick.mjs` remains, as an entry-point shim that starts the same run. A member's `.github/workflows/claudinite-scheduler.yml` names the module by literal path, and that file is the one path a converge cannot push — it is staged and lands as a pull request somebody merges — so every member runs the refreshed mount from its old workflow for a while. A missing entry point there is not a broken task; it is that repo's whole queue stopping with no run left to notice it. `scheduler-workflow-shape` accepts either spelling for the same window, and a test pins both so neither can be tidied away. They retire when no member's workflow still names `tick.mjs` — read the members' files, don't guess a date.

Two things outside the rename that the sweep turned up, neither acted on:

- **`docs/per-project-scheduling/` is not obsolete** and was not deleted. ~45 live source files cite it for contracts the queue explicitly did not replace — §1 (the task declaration contract, the outcome ceiling), §2 (anchors), §3 (discovery, hash-minute, signals), §6 (the task classification table). Reasoning on [#1108](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1108).
- Historical records were left alone: that directory's `MIGRATION.md`, migration modules, and the `old-workflows` rehearsal fixture, which is supposed to hold the genuine old text and now does.

Both done, in one PR: **[#1108](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1108)** — CI green on `e0a1f4c` (tests, both conformance sweeps, the growth gate).

## [#877](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/877) — the rename

**`schedulerRun`**, per your call. Recorded as DESIGN decision 27, closing decision 21. `queue/tick.mjs` → `queue/scheduler-run.mjs`, `planTick` → `planSchedulerRun`, `stubs/claudinite-tick.yml` → `stubs/claudinite-scheduler.yml`, and the vocabulary swept across [DESIGN](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/claude/executor-loop-question-nyfelg/docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md), SCENARIOS, RESEARCH, the simulator, the workflows and the pack prose — 98 files, 2347 tests green.

One deliberate exception to your closing condition: **`queue/tick.mjs` stays, as an entry-point shim.** A member's scheduler workflow names the module by literal path, and `.github/workflows/` is the one path a converge cannot push — so every member runs the refreshed mount from its old workflow for a while, and a missing entry point there stops that repo's whole queue with nothing left to notice it. `scheduler-workflow-shape` accepts either spelling for the same window, and a test pins both so neither gets tidied away.

**I did not delete `docs/per-project-scheduling/`** — your assumption that it's all obsolete doesn't hold. About 45 live source files cite it as the authority for contracts the queue explicitly did *not* replace: `task-contract.mjs` (§1, the declaration contract), `calendar.mjs` (§2, anchors), `discover.mjs`/`hash-minute.mjs`/`signals/*` (§3), `verify-outcome.mjs` (the outcome ceiling), and every pack's task header (§6, the classification table). tasks-dispatch DESIGN's own opening names those as untouched and supersedes only §3–§5's slot machinery. What *is* stale is narrower than the directory — the slot sections — and clearing it properly means lifting the live contracts into their own home, not a delete. Say the word and I'll open that.

## [#801](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/801) — the fan-in box

Built it minimally and it ran in **67 seconds**: [#1101](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1101) and [#1102](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1102) as fan-out, [#1103](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1103) `Blocked-by` both. #1103 stayed blocked through the first close, then at 12:50:29Z took *"Released: #1102 has closed, and nothing else holds this item"* — **from the closing side, not a scheduler run** — and closed 25 seconds later. That's S18 live and the close-time-release gap I flagged on #883, both shut.

It also caught a real defect: the janitor parked #1101 `needs-human` **eight seconds after that item closed clean**. Its stateless repair rules over a snapshot, and an item mid-swap is indistinguishable from one whose swap tore — so finished work got a triage label and a comment asking a human to re-queue it. #1089 widened that window a lot (claim→close is now ~4s, runs back to back). Filed as [#1104](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1104) and fixed in the same PR by confirming before acting; I watched both new tests fail without the guard.

## What I couldn't do

**#1089 has reached no member.** I checked GoogleCalendarEventCreator directly — no `heartbeat.mjs`, `suspend.mjs`, `readiness.mjs` or `converge-item.mjs` in its mount, executor workflow still `timeout-minutes: 50`, drain still running an executor inline. You picked "force the fleet now" and I tried; `missingbulb/Shepherd` is outside this session's repo scope and attaching it was denied. So this one is yours to press, or mine once Shepherd is attached:

```
missingbulb/Shepherd → Actions → Claudinite scheduler → Run workflow
  branch: main
  wake: fleet-baseline
```

Tonight's 02:00Z converge delivers the mount half anyway; the workflow half lands as a per-member PR either way. That should have happened when #1089 merged and didn't — my miss.

> ⚠️ Still open: [#1108](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1108) is green and waiting on your review. [#801](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/801)'s last box — #1089's workflow pieces observed on one member — needs the Shepherd dispatch above, which I can't reach. # Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, name the folders the change touched** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Leave out test folders, README edits, and above all any file whose diff is comments only.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

- do-later: File a change to be made AFTER the work in flight — a well-defined issue, marked for the queue and blocked behind the current PR/issue and behind the previous deferral, so repeated asks chain. Use when the owner says "/do-later …", "do this after this lands", or otherwise defers a change instead of derailing the session.
- extract-from-activity: Mine a window of a repo's commits, merged PRs and issue activity for durable, reusable lessons and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from repo artifacts — the growth-extract task's activity half, or an owner asking what a recent stretch of work taught.
- extract-from-conversations: Mine an agent-user conversation — a captured conversation log or the live session — for friction-driven lessons (misunderstandings, backtracks, measured wall-time waits) and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from a session transcript or the conversation-logs branch, or when an owner asks for a retrospective.
- file-placement: Where a file should live — the reference-distance metric, the high-reach code smell, and the mandated-location, test-location and plugin-contract exemptions. Use before placing, moving, or renaming a file, or when reviewing where one lives.
- generate-project-instructions: Decompose a project into its pack facets (working-style class, technology, aspect, domain) and extract its working instructions into reusable canon packs plus the project's own local packs (.claudinite/local_packs/). Use when a project has no established working style yet, or it exhibits a facet no pack covers — during bootstrap of a fresh/empty repo, or on an uplevel request.
- growth-dedup: Prune a repo's local packs of items the mounted Claudinite canon now covers — remove, strip to residue, or track a wording drift, never grow an entry. Use when the growth dedup task runs, or when asked to reconcile or dedup local packs against the canon.
- prose-to-checks: Mine pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. Use when auditing packs for convertible rules, when the weekly prose-to-checks sweep runs, or as the upgrade pass over prose a growth-extract run just wrote.
- repo-text-sweeps: Mechanics for grep/sed sweeps, renames, and path relocations across a repo. Use before a bulk find-replace, a rename, or moving files — and after one, to catch silently broken references.
- single-branch-status: Assess one branch's landed status — merged, already-in-main, superseded, orphaned, or genuine unmerged work — read-only. Use when triaging whether a single branch is safe to delete, judging by content not the ref's name (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-branches task hands you branches to assess).
- single-issue-triage: Triage one open issue and take the first applicable action — close-if-implemented, needs-decision, blocked, quick-win, or leave. Use when acting on a single issue; "implemented in main" must be verified against main's current content and the default is to comment, not close (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-issues task hands you issues to triage).
- single-pr-status: Assess one open pull request's landed status — keep-open, or closeable (merged, already-in-main, superseded, stale) — read-only. Use when triaging whether a single PR should stay open, judging by its commits and diff not its title (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-prs task hands you PRs to assess).
- unattended-agents: Architecture and practices for unattended, automation-invoked agents and recurring routines. Use when building, structuring, or running an AI agent, a scheduled routine, or a multi-stage agent pipeline.
- verify-in-production: Decide whether a change that just landed can only be proven in production, and if so file the verification that comes back on its own once it is live. Use at the end of every change, beside the conversation capture — not on request.
- writing-claudinite-skills: Authoring or changing a skill in the Claudinite corpus — SKILL.md conventions, where a skill's checks and tests live, catalog and pack wiring. Use when creating or editing a pack's skills/<name>/ in the canon; a consumer project's own agent docs are authoring-agent-docs' turf.
- writing-migration-plans: How to order the phases of an implementation or migration plan so nothing stalls mid-run — front-load the out-of-band setup, collapse the review gates into one stacked-PR pass, leave only executable steps — and how to keep its tracking issue append-only while implementing. Use when writing or reviewing a migration plan or a phased implementation plan, and when working through one's tracking issue.
- writing-tasks: The contract a Claudinite task is written to — the declaration's fields, the code-work and agentic phases, the precondition as the only decision point, ordering, and how a work item converges. Use when writing or changing a tasks/<name>/task.mjs or its worker, or when a task-declaration check fires.
- writing-tests: Practices for writing tests you can trust. Use before writing or changing any test — see-it-fail discipline, snapshot/golden rules, CI-only and heavy-browser tests, fuzzy-metric gating.
- design: Create a design canvas — a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including Markdown ones — format is part of the design pass, never a speed shortcut.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, handing the viewer a file to save, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. - code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. - simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). # Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with.
