# Merge to main

If the project's own `CLAUDE.md` names a merge-policy file, that file overrides the divergent
points below (merge method, CI gating). Don't go hunting for one it doesn't name.

1. Load `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request` in one `ToolSearch`.

4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Don't pre-read
   mergeability; the call fails loudly.

Don't re-read the issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge.

{"total_count":6,"workflow_runs":[{"id":32375653687,"name":"CI","display_title":"The tick becomes the scheduler run, and the janitor stops parking finished work","workflow_id":317526095,"run_number":1074,"run_attempt":1,"event":"pull_request","status":"in_progress","head_branch":"claude/executor-loop-question-nyfelg","head_sha":"4caeddce81c8df197cad8ae0cb6051c81e4bdb3b","head_commit":{"message":"tasks-dispatch: rename the tick to the scheduler run

The owner's naming rule rejects single nouns that need contextual reading, and
"the tick" was the last one left. `schedulerRun` over `generatorRun`: the slot
scheduler is gone, so the word names one thing again — the repo's one cron
workflow, which is what runs it — while "the generator" is the role's name in
DESIGN §2 and §5 rather than a run's.

`queue/tick.mjs` stays as an entry-point shim. A member's scheduler workflow
names the module by literal path and `.github/workflows/` is the one path a
converge cannot push, so every member runs the refreshed mount from the old
workflow for a while; a missing entry point there stops that repo's queue with
no run left to fix it. `scheduler-workflow-shape` accepts either spelling for
the same window, and the rehearsal's old-workflows fixture now carries the old
entry point so the window is proven rather than assumed.

Closes #877
Refs #801

heartbeat, the hold, and the two bounds they retire

The heartbeat (§15.15): the executor comments on its own item every 15
minutes while the work step runs, so long work is legal rather than dark.
With it, the tick's reclaim stops measuring the ISSUE's silence and measures
the HOLDER's — its last live claim or heartbeat — which is #924: any comment
moved `updated_at`, including the one an executor that lost the claim race
writes on its way out, so the reclaim of an item nobody held kept deferring.
A struck claim is not a sign of life.

Two rationales the heartbeat invalidates are rewritten rather than left
standing: the run cap that used to bound a work step (leases.mjs), and
code-work's claim that overlap with a zombie is excluded by construction
(code-work-run.mjs) — it no longer is, and re-entrancy is what covers it,
which is why the contract asks for re-entrancy and not idempotency.

The tick/drain decoupling (§15.16): the drain job dispatches the executor
workflow instead of being one, so it leaves the tick's concurrency group. It
therefore runs no task code, which is why the tick stub's secrets marker
goes — and why `withDeclaredSecrets` now stamps at the marker or not at all.
Its old fallback would have stamped every task secret into the one job the
design says must never hold one.

The operator hold (§15.24): one repo variable, stamped into all four
workflows, checked as the first act of both entry points — before the config
load, before the first API call. It gates STARTS, not running work.

A dead chain now escalates: after three consecutive deaths the continuation
stops re-dispatching and says so on the workflow-failure issue, because a
queue that has quietly stopped draining is the one failure where every
individual run looks like an ordinary death.

Refs #883, Refs the executor's run shape: one item, a random head, a checked dispatch

The tests that pinned the pre-review contract went with it — `the loop stops
at maxItems` asserted the thing that is no longer true. What replaces it
asserts the structure: three pickable items of DIFFERENT titles (so the
same-title mutex is not what stops the run) and one settled; a chain that
continues only after a settle, and stands down after a lost race; and the
dispatch judged by status, since a 403 returns a body that reads fine.

Pick order gets a property test rather than a fixed order — a pinned order
would pass against a comparator that never shuffles.

Refs #883"},"path":".github/workflows/ci.yml","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/32354875035","pull_requests":[1108],"actor":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"triggering_actor":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"created_at":"2026-08-20T09:38:05Z","updated_at":"2026-08-20T09:39:23Z","run_started_at":"2026-08-20T09:38:05Z"}]}
